1: On a peaceful afternoon along the Pittsburgh riverfront, someone aims a sniper rifle from atop a parking garage.
2: Six shots ring out in mere seconds, leaving five innocent civilians dead on the spot.
3: Instead of confessing, the arrested suspect simply writes one name on a piece of paper: Jack Reacher.
4: A white van pulls into downtown Pittsburgh as the driver loads handmade bullets with gloved hands.
5: On the top floor of the parking garage, the man feeds a coin into the meter and knocks over a cone as he parks.
6: With shell casings and a coin left at the scene alongside security footage of the white van, Detective Emerson quickly tracks down the culprit.
7: While inspecting the crime scene, Emerson recovers a fingerprint from the coin inside the parking meter.
8: The print belongs to former Army sniper James Barr, and police even find the rifle used in the attack at his home.
9: As District Attorney Rodin looks on, Barr is left with only two choices: life in prison or the death penalty.
10: Yet even after sixteen hours of interrogation, Barr refuses to speak and writes a single name on a notepad instead.
11: Jack Reacher is a heavily decorated former military police investigator who vanished off the grid after leaving the service two years ago.
12: At that same moment at a bus station, Reacher sees Barr's face on the news and heads straight for Pittsburgh.
13: Just then, the office door swings open.
14: Reacher visits the hospital room of Barr, who lies in a coma after being brutally beaten by fellow inmates during transport.
15: There he meets Barr's defense attorney, Helen, who happens to be District Attorney Rodin's daughter.
16: Running into Reacher in the hospital hallway, Helen assumes he has come to help Barr.
17: Meanwhile, a man named Linsky at a cement plant urgently calls someone to ask who Jack Reacher is.
18: Sitting across from him at a diner, Helen vows to save Barr from the death penalty, but Reacher remains cold and indifferent.
19: Reacher reveals to Helen that Barr had previously gone on a shooting spree in Iraq as well.
20: The incident was covered up because the slain private contractors were gang rapists, a story Reacher continues to tell as he walks toward the bus terminal.
21: Having promised to track Barr down if he ever killed again, Reacher has come not to help him, but to punish him himself.
22: Reacher heads to the bus terminal as if his business here is already finished.
23: Helen stops Reacher just as he is about to board the bus, telling him to become her investigator if he wants to see the evidence, which he accepts on one condition.
24: Helen goes to visit the victims' families while Reacher inspects the shooting scene on his own.
25: Helen visits the father of one of the victims, explaining that she wants to know what kind of person his daughter was.
26: Standing before the memorial bouquets by the river, Reacher walks over to the exact spot where the sniper took aim.
27: As Reacher stands in the parking garage, something strange catches his eye.
28: Looking out from an overpass, Reacher realizes this spot would have been a far better vantage point for a sniper.
29: However, Helen is met with the father's fury as he demands to know why she is defending the man who murdered his daughter.
30: Meanwhile, upon learning that his daughter has taken on the case, the District Attorney tries to stop Helen.
31: When Reacher visits the evidence room, Emerson shows him what appears to be an airtight set of clues.
32: As Reacher hefts the sniper rifle in the evidence room, Emerson boasts that the investigation was flawless.
33: At a bar that night, a young woman named Sandy approaches Reacher.
34: Reacher sits alone eating dinner at the bar, unaware that someone is watching him closely.
35: Sandy brazenly tries to seduce Reacher, asking him to go somewhere quiet with her.
36: Sensing a trap, Reacher turns her down, prompting a group of men claiming to be Sandy's brothers to pick a fight with him.
37: Outside the bar on the rain-slicked street, five men surround Reacher.
38: All five men lunged at him at once, but Reacher takes every single one of them down in seconds.
39: However, the police arrive suspiciously fast, revealing that the whole brawl was a trap set specifically for Reacher.
40: Taken into custody and locked in a holding cell, Reacher gets an angry lecture from Helen for hurting those men.
41: Emerson hands Helen the serial number of Barr's rifle, the exact detail Reacher had asked about in the evidence room.
42: Reacher is convinced that the bar fight was an orchestrated trap meant to run him out of town.
43: Helen shares the backgrounds of the victims: a nanny, a janitor, a wife, an investment broker, and a construction company owner named Oline.
44: They were just ordinary people going about their day—a wife buying a tenth-anniversary gift, a janitor getting tickets to his son's baseball game, and an investment broker carrying flowers.
45: While washing his shirt in front of Helen in his motel room, Reacher points out something suspicious in the victims' stories.
46: Reacher argues that the victims were not all gathered at that spot by mere coincidence.
47: In a shadowy mansion sits an old man known as the Zec, the true mastermind behind the shooting.
48: As his henchman Charlie watches, Linsky confesses that his attempt to scare Reacher off ended in failure.
49: The Zec, a survivor of a Siberian gulag, subjects his blundering subordinate to a gruesome test of survival.
50: When Linsky fails to bite off his own fingers, Charlie shoots him dead, and the Zec names Reacher as their next target.
51: Combing through Barr's credit card statements, Reacher becomes certain that Barr drove to a distant shooting range every weekend.
52: As the two set out on the road to retrace Barr's steps, Reacher remarks that Barr could not have been alone that day.
53: Reacher tracks down Sandy from the bar, and she confesses that a man named Jeb paid her a hundred dollars to set him up.
54: Reacher warns Sandy to get out of town and stay hidden for a while.
55: Driving Jeb's red car toward the man's house, Reacher is closely watched from afar by Charlie.
56: Reacher arrives at Jeb's house, only to find two men waiting to ambush him with baseball bats.
57: Hiding inside the bathroom, the two men suddenly lunge out at Reacher.
58: After overpowering both attackers and learning that Jeb packed up and vanished right after getting out of jail, Reacher is convinced that Jeb is already dead.
59: Back at Helen's office, Reacher begins to explain why Barr's skill level doesn't match the crime scene.
60: Reacher points out that a shooter of Barr's limited ability could never have hit moving targets while staring directly into the sun from that spot.
61: A real sniper would have shot from the bridge, where there was no need to park a car or feed a meter.
62: Frustrated by his seemingly absurd claim of Barr's innocence, Helen yells at Reacher to leave, only for him to point out the window at the carefree people on the street.
63: Reacher then spots a silver car tailing him outside the window, and a license plate check reveals it belongs to Lebendauer Enterprises.
64: The moment Helen runs the plates, the Zec immediately contacts Charlie.
65: The only real target was Oline, the construction company owner, while the other four victims were merely collateral damage to disguise the assassination.
66: The second shot fired was the one that killed Oline, the single bullet the sniper took the most care to aim.
67: Nevertheless, Helen draws a line, insisting that catching the real killer is not her job as a defense attorney.
68: That night, Charlie approaches Sandy claiming to be a friend of Jeb's and murders her on the spot.
69: At the courthouse the next day, Helen finds Reacher and tells him she has located a shooting range in Ohio that Barr likely frequented.
70: When the police name Reacher as the prime suspect in Sandy's murder and raid his motel, he narrowly escapes.
71: From inside a parked car, Reacher watches Emerson question the motel guests.
72: While pursuing Charlie, Reacher ends up being chased by the police himself until he finally slips into a crowd at a bus stop.
73: After a high-speed chase tearing through tunnels and alleys, Reacher ditches his car and blends into the crowd waiting at a bus stop.
74: The District Attorney and Emerson show up at Helen's apartment to demand answers about Reacher's whereabouts.
75: Calling Helen from a payphone, Reacher warns her that someone has been tailing him since his very first day in town.
76: Reacher travels to the shooting range in Ohio, which is run by an elderly former Marine named Cash.
77: At first, Cash feigns ignorance and claims he doesn't know anyone named Barr.
78: Cash agrees to talk only if Reacher can hit three bullseyes, prompting Reacher to lie prone on the firing line.
79: Taking aim from the prone position, Reacher misses his first shot slightly before driving the next two rounds dead center.
80: Cash brings out Barr's best target sheet, but Reacher immediately tells him that the holes were faked at point-blank range.
81: Security footage from the shooting range reveals the man who accompanied Barr: Charlie, the very same man who murdered Sandy.
82: In the District Attorney's office, Helen hands her father files exposing the corruption behind Lebendauer Enterprises.
83: After listening to Helen's findings, the District Attorney simply replies that he is placing her into protective custody.
84: In the elevator, Helen runs into Detective Emerson, who turns out to be working for the Zec and kidnaps her on the spot.
85: When Reacher calls Helen's phone, it is Charlie who answers on the other end.
86: Charlie uses Helen as bait to lure him in, but Reacher refuses to be intimidated and hangs up after promising to come for him on his own terms.
87: Heading to the quarry where Helen is being held hostage, Reacher brings Cash along to provide sniper cover.
88: Before dawn at the quarry, Cash hands Reacher only a hunting knife while he lies prone with his rifle.
89: At that same moment inside, the Zec orders Helen to call her father and coerce him into dropping the investigation.
90: Just then, Reacher calls again from outside the quarry and promises Helen that he is coming to rescue her.
91: As Reacher's car barrels into the quarry under a hail of gunfire from all sides, the rescue plan goes sideways right from the start.
92: Ducking inside the bullet-riddled car, Reacher grabs a single knife and leaps out into the darkness.
93: After taking out the enemies inside a trailer, Reacher picks off the guards one by one as he advances toward the main office.
94: The lights in the office suddenly go out, and Emerson presses his gun to Helen's head.
95: Coming face-to-face in the pouring rain, Reacher and Charlie cast their guns aside and clash in a brutal bare-knuckle brawl.
96: After taking Charlie down for good, Reacher heads straight for the office where Helen is being held.
97: Reacher takes down Emerson, the corrupt cop who had planted Barr's fingerprint on the parking meter coin and was holding Helen at gunpoint.
98: Realizing that Emerson was the traitor all along, Helen regrets ever having doubted her father.
99: Left alone as the final mastermind, the Zec scoffs that an old man like him will easily walk free even if he is sent to prison.
100: While Helen calls the police, Reacher bypasses the law and executes the Zec in his own ruthless way.
101: When Barr wakes up in his hospital bed and Helen asks for the truth, he has no memory of the shooting itself but says he would have done it differently.
102: Looking at the crime scene photos from his hospital bed, Barr explains that he would have parked the van on the highway to keep the sun at his back.
103: Refusing Helen's offer of protection, Barr brings up a certain man who promised to come and punish him if he ever crossed the line again.
104: That very man who vowed to hunt Barr down if he ever caused trouble again—and ended up clearing his name instead—boards a bus once more and rides off into the unknown.
105: That was *Jack Reacher*, directed by Christopher McQuarrie, starring Tom Cruise as a drifter investigator who chooses true justice over the law.
106: In the end, the man who saved an innocent suspect from a frame-up was the very person who had come to execute him, so let us know in the comments whether you think Reacher's way of justice was right.
